schema_version.description: Schema version. v1 only; future versions are rejected so older code fails closed against newer configs (a forward-compat upgrade requires a new code release that recognizes the new const).

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when migrate.py --apply completed against this repo. Sole writer is migrate.py itself; SKILL.md wrappers must never set this independently.

from_layout.description: Originating layout that was migrated. Only known historical value is 'docs+tdd' (the pre-workflow-cleanup layout); null means no migration has occurred.

offered_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when first-run preflight last offered to set up branch protection. Used to suppress repeated prompts.

applied_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when branch protection was successfully applied via gh api.

declined.description: True if user explicitly declined branch protection setup. Suppresses future prompts permanently until manually flipped.

profile.description: Named protection profile applied. Only known value today is 'team-pr-1approval-noforce' (PR required, 1 approval, no force-push).

ci.description: Continuous-integration posture for this repo. Read by the tp-pr-iterate loop's CI-settle wait (loop_driver._ci_settled_on_head).

expects_github_checks.description: Whether this repo expects GitHub-hosted check-runs on its PRs. Default (absent) is true — an empty statusCheckRollup is treated as 'CI not settled yet' (fail-closed). Set false when CI runs locally / off-GitHub (self-hosted-ci-runner): an empty rollup then counts as settled so the review loop converges instead of spinning to a cap. Only affects empty rollups; a non-empty rollup is evaluated normally regardless.

gate_command.description: The repo's local CI gate command. Null = offered and declined; an absent key = never offered. A non-empty string names the command the local gate runs (e.g. the pytest invocation).

review.description: Code-review posture for this repo. Read by the tp-pr-iterate loop's two-stable success terminal (loop_driver._expects_copilot_review).

expects_copilot.description: Whether GitHub Copilot code review is an available reviewer on this repo's PRs. Default (absent) is true — the two-stable terminal requires copilot_reviewed_successfully as its third conjunct, so a Copilot-reviewed repo never converges on an absent/stale Copilot signal. Set false when Copilot code review is NOT attachable (e.g. an individual account with no Copilot entitlement — a structural absence, distinct from a transient 'Copilot encountered an error' review): the loop is already dual-source, so the /code-review arm then carries the terminal on its own (codereview-clean + zero unresolved actionable threads + the minor-only classifier flip) instead of spinning to cap-exhausted. Only DROPS the Copilot conjunct; the /code-review and ground-truth-thread conjuncts are unchanged, so convergence is never weakened into a false positive.

require_human_approval.description: Whether the deterministic merge gate requires a current human-approval (a current APPROVED human review on the head) as its fifth predicate. Default (absent) is true — the gate folds pred_human_approved strictly, so the autonomous path can never cross the irreversible `gh pr merge` boundary without an explicit, out-of-band human approval current on the head SHA. Set false only to OPT OUT of the human-approval predicate (the other four predicates still gate); the predicate is then OMITTED from evaluate_gate and the pre-change four-predicate fold is unchanged. IMPORTANT: setting false opts out of the gate predicate, but land.py still hard-refuses unattended landing at the land boundary — the opt-out never crosses the irreversible boundary without a human approving at HEAD. The flag is read from committed HEAD only (via `git show HEAD:`), so an uncommitted edit cannot change this value. The predicate is read by deterministic_gate.evaluate_gate via human_approval._require_human_approval. Deny-rule residual: the permissions.deny rule Bash(git commit --no-verify:*) uses a prefix match and cannot block '--no-verify' appearing after other arguments; prose prohibitions (CLAUDE.md, commit-after-work.md) and reviewer inspection remain the backstop for those forms.

automation_identities.description: Optional additional automation logins (lowercased) treated as NON-human by the human-approval predicate, beyond the hardcoded floor (github-actions[bot], dependabot[bot], the Copilot REST logins) and the framework's own resolved self-login. Use this for committing CI service accounts so a review submitted by such an account never satisfies pred_human_approved (separation-of-duties / multi-account SoD). Each entry is matched case-insensitively against the review author's login. A non-list value is ignored gracefully.

approval_survives_safe_base_sync.description: Whether an approval / proof-of-review digest anchored on a PRE-base-sync head is still trusted after one or more CERTIFIED mechanical base-sync merges have moved the head forward. Default (absent) is false — the strict INVERSE of this block's other defaults, because here the strict default IS off (an opt-in relaxation, not a strict-default fold). True ONLY on the literal boolean `true`; absence, a corrupt/non-dict `review` block, or any truthy-non-bool value (1, "true", ...) all fold to false. Each certified link is independently re-proven from git objects alone (merge shape, second-parent-on-base, an allowlisted merge-tree recompute, byte-equality outside the conflict set, and a resolver byte-reproduction over a zero-drop backstop) by `skills/_shared/base_sync_cert.py` — no PR comment, local state file, or producer claim is ever an input to the verdict. Read from the COMMITTED HEAD only (via the existing `_load_repo_config` path, same as `require_human_approval`) — an uncommitted edit cannot enable the carry. See `three-pillars-docs/tp-designs/approval-survives-safe-base-sync/detailed-design.md` and `skills/_shared/repo-config.md`.

base_sync_carry_max_chain.description: The maximum number of certified base-sync merges the carry's first-parent walk will cross while searching for a matching anchor (the approval's or proof digest's original head). Default (absent, out-of-range, or wrong-typed, including bool) is 5. Only consulted when approval_survives_safe_base_sync is true; a chain longer than this cap fails closed with a re-approve-on-current-head remediation, never an unsound PASS.

strata_finder_segment.description: Segmenting of a large diff for Strata review finders (skills/tp-pr-iterate/scripts/finder_segments.py). A diff over max_lines changed lines or max_files files runs one Strata finder per segment, serially, at most max_segments segments per angle; the rest are skipped and the Opus check re-reads them. Defaults 600 / 10 / 4. `false` turns segmenting off. Inert off Strata.

living_doc_handres_preserves_approval.description: Whether the living-doc hand-resolution carry (living_doc_carry.certify_link_carry) may certify a base-sync link without byte-exact reproduction. Default (absent) is true — default-ON, and only consulted when approval_survives_safe_base_sync is true. False ONLY on the literal boolean `false` (living_doc_carry.carry_livingdoc_handres_enabled): the operator's opt-out back to the strict byte-exact carry. Read from the COMMITTED HEAD via the gate's _load_repo_config, so it must be declared here or the schema prune drops it and the opt-out is silently ignored.

require_ci_local_stamp.description: Whether the deterministic merge gate requires a current local CI stamp (a passing gate_command run recorded against the head) as a predicate. Default (absent) is false; set true to make a fresh local CI stamp a gate conjunct on consumer repos that run CI locally.

require_review_proof.description: Whether the merge gate requires a proof-of-review digest (the carried approval / proof-of-review digest) as a predicate. Default (absent) is false; a consumer repo that carries a proof-of-review digest sets this true so the gate folds the carry predicate in.

proof_dir.description: Where tp-pr-iterate writes its review-proof artifacts, overriding the default under the git dir (review_proof_root.resolve). Absolute, or relative to the repo root.

instructions_declined.description: True if the operator declined the review-instructions offer (e.g. the per-reviewer angle / instructions onboarding). Sticky — suppresses re-offering the instructions on subsequent runs.

proof_dir.description: Optional /tp-pr-iterate proof-root override, RELATIVE to the worktree root (this file is committed, so an absolute value is refused with a notice and the default is used). Default: <absolute git-dir>/three-pillars/review-proof, outside the working tree. An absolute root comes only from the uncommitted TP_REVIEW_PROOF_DIR env var. Resolved by skills/tp-pr-iterate/scripts/proof_root.py.

angles.description: tp-pr-iterate review angles as data (angles.load_angles). Absent = the three default Opus confirmers. Reviews are always Opus.

pdw.description: parallel-design-worktrees configuration: loop guards, URL allowlist for fix-comments, and runner backend selector.

diff_growth_multiplier.description: DEPRECATED and unread (the retired loop growth guard); kept so existing configs validate. Use growth_multiplier.

round_cap.description: Counted review rounds after which a round with blocking findings stops at budget-exhausted/round-cap (round_budget.tick). Default 3 (2 under review-weight just-do-it). Raise it and re-run to lift the terminal.

growth_multiplier.description: Three-dot diff total vs. the round-1 baseline at which the loop stops at budget-exhausted/growth-lines. Default 1.5.

test_code_ratio.description: Loop-added test lines vs. code lines at which the loop stops at budget-exhausted/test-code-ratio (with ratio_floor_lines). Default 3.0.

ratio_floor_lines.description: Minimum loop-added test lines before test_code_ratio can fire. Default 100.

growth_floor_lines.description: Minimum three-dot diff total (added + deleted lines) before growth_multiplier and test_code_ratio are judged. Default 300.

wall_clock_sec.description: Seconds since started_at after which the loop stops at cap-exhausted/wall-clock. Default 14400.

k_consecutive.description: Number of consecutive structural-present rounds that triggers convergence-failure. Default 3.

idle_timeout_sec.description: Seconds with no new comments after a non-structural verdict before transitioning to awaiting-human-review. Default 1800.

comment_url_allowlist.description: Additional URL netlocs allowed in fix-comment bodies beyond github.com and the repo origin host.

type.description: Runner backend identifier. v1 supports 'claude' only — `run_supervisor._wrap_slash` raises NotImplementedError on any other value, so the schema fails the misconfig at validation time rather than at runtime. The `local-run-auto-sessions` design will broaden this enum.

fleet.description: Fleet-level configuration for worktree-isolation guards and related tunables.

diff_balloon_factor.description: Multiplier vs. base diff size at which the diff-balloon guard fires and rejects the candidate. Default 5.

github.description: PR-author bot-account configuration. The USERNAME is non-secret and committable; the credential NEVER lands here — it stays in the operator's gh keyring and is read ephemerally (gh auth token --user).

pr_author_account.description: GitHub login the framework authors PRs as. Null = feature unconfigured (bare gh pr create, ambient auth).

used_for.description: Which PR-creation sites author as the bot. all-prs = tp-design-complete manual path AND tp-run-full-design Tier 6; autonomous-only = Tier 6 only.

review_requests.description: Human logins requested as reviewers on bot-authored PRs (gh pr create --reviewer). Empty/absent = no auto-request from the helper.

verified_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the account was last verified present in the gh keyring (gh auth token --user succeeded).

offered_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when first-run last offered this setup.

declined.description: True if the operator declined the offer. Sticky — suppresses re-prompt.

forge.description: What this repo's origin is (forge-interface). Written once by skills/_shared/forge_config.py::record_kind on first-run detection, or by the operator when the origin is an ssh alias / custom-port Gitea that detection cannot classify (set web_base alone). Read by forge.resolve and by first-run conditions 3 and 7. No credential ever lands here — a Gitea token stays in the operator's tea config / env.

kind.description: The forge class. Recorded once — record_kind never overwrites it. `other` silences the `no web base` setup line.

host.description: The origin host as parsed from the remote URL (an ssh alias stays the alias). Audit trail for the recorded kind; never used to classify.

web_base.description: Instance base (scheme + host + port) for a forge detection cannot reach — the ssh-alias / custom-port Gitea setup. An operator-written value is MERGED into, never replaced. Highest-priority web-base source in forge.resolve.

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the kind was recorded.

local_implement.description: Opt-in per-task cheap-tier dispatch for /tp-phase-implement --local and /tp-run-full-design --local. Absent block = feature off; every key is optional and merged over local_implement_config.DEFAULTS.

enabled.description: Master switch. --local is refused unless true.

model.description: Model the eligibility gate's `local` rung spawns tp-task-worker with.

fallback_model.description: Model of the `sonnet` rung (the first escalation; a `--cheap-tier` run without `--local` starts there).

default_run_flag.description: "on" makes launch_design_run.py forward --local on every launch (when enabled and full_design are also true and the runaway-ceiling capability gate passes); --no-local removes it for one run. Unset = off.

escalate.description: On exhausted retries, escalate the task to the next rung (local -> sonnet -> opus) instead of halting.

max_retries.description: Same-tier retries after a verify FAIL, with the failing output fed back.

max_files.description: A task listing more Files than this is classified `sonnet`, never `local`.

registry_files.description: Repo-relative registry paths a task may edit mechanically (1-3 added lines, no deletions) without failing `unlisted file`; the edit is logged instead.

client_timeouts.description: Record of the client-timeout settings the orphan reaper's first-run offer applied or declined (local_timeouts.py). `values` holds any subset of the four env keys; `{}` is the decline record.

role_engines.description: Deprecated (one-cheap-engine): the engine follows the run (Sonnet, or Strata under --local) and a set key only adds a deprecation note. Engine per routable role for the local-role-routing design (skills/_shared/role_engine.py). Four keys: `council_member`, `review_finder`, `context_scout`, `explainer`; each takes `local` or `opus`, and only `explainer: opus` still acts (Opus drafts every kind). An unset `context_scout` follows `review_finder`. Judgment roles (synthesizer, final check, auditors) have no key here and always run on Opus. Absent block = every role on the run's cheap engine.

council_member.description: Engine for a council persona. Unset = `opus`.

review_finder.description: Engine for a PR-review finder angle. Unset = `opus`.

context_scout.description: Engine for the context scout. Unset = follows `review_finder` (a scout reads what a finder reads).

explainer.description: Drafting engine for the explainer (skills/_shared/explainer/, resolved by explain_engine; the drafter is a cheap site under one-cheap-engine). Unset = the run's cheap engine drafts: Sonnet, or Strata under --local. `local` = deprecated and changes nothing: the drafter follows the run, Strata under --local and Sonnet when there is no backend, when the slot is busy or when the run is not --local. `opus` = Opus drafts every kind (the one value that still acts). The Opus check is fixed and has no key.

The explainer's switches (explainer-agent), read by skills/_shared/explainer/explain_config.py, which merges the block over its defaults and drops each bad entry with one warning. The drafting engine is `role_engines.explainer`, not this block. Absent block = every default (explainer on, artifact publishing on, no override).

enabled.description: The off switch. Default `true`. `false` turns the explainer off: no brief, no explained ruling, and today's PR flow byte-identically.

publish_artifact.description: Default `true`: publish the HTML page as a private claude.ai artifact when the Artifact tool exists. `false` keeps the local HTML only.

drafter_override.description: Per-kind drafter pin; wins over `role_engines.explainer` for its kind. Only the two Opus-checked kinds take a key, and the only value is `opus`. Empty = no override.

strata_spawn.description: Strata-routed spawn policy: the busy-slot policy (`strata_spawn.py`), the permission rules a child launch adds (`child_permissions.py`) and the child Bash-sandbox switch (`child_sandbox.py`). Absent block = `fallback`, no extra rules, sandbox `off`.

busy.description: `fallback` (default): a busy slot spawns at once and the Sonnet-served reply is accepted. `wait`: poll the slot, never use Sonnet, halt at the overall ceiling.

permissions.description: Rules a child launch ADDS to its shipped lists (`child_permissions.py`). An entry that is not a rule string warns and is skipped; the shipped deny list can never be removed from here.

allow_extra.description: Extra `--allowedTools` rules (`Tool` or `Tool(matcher)`) for this repo's children.

deny_extra.description: Extra `--disallowedTools` rules. Additions only — the shipped deny list stays whole.

sandbox.description: The child Bash sandbox (`child_sandbox.py`). `off` (default, shipped): no sandbox merge. `on`: a site-S1 child launch merges the sandbox block into the attempt worktree's local settings. `TP_CHILD_SANDBOX=on|off` overrides it for one run.

plan_audit.description: Plan-audit prechecks run before the Slot 6 reader (plan_couplings.py). Absent block = no couplings declared.

couplings.description: File-coupling rules (plan_couplings.py check (a)): when a task creates a new file matching `when_new` (glob), it must also list `requires_listed` in its File field.

when_new.description: Glob (fnmatch) for a newly-created file that triggers the coupling.

requires_listed.description: Repo-relative path that must also appear in the same task's File list.

merge_from_main.description: /tp-merge-from-main settings. Absent block = generated-file conflicts defer as before (no regenerate resolver).

generators.description: Generated files the regenerate resolver may rebuild instead of deferring a conflict on them: each declares the file path and the argv that regenerates it.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the generated file the generator owns.

write.description: argv (run from the repo root, no shell) that regenerates the file in place.

check.description: Optional argv (run from the repo root, no shell) that exits 0 when the file is up to date.

timeout.description: Seconds the write/check argv may run before the resolver gives up on this generator.

inputs.description: Repo-relative source files whose conflicts this generator can resolve by regenerating.

cwd.description: Repo-relative directory the write/check argv runs in instead of the repo root.

generator_offer.description: Record of the lockfile-catalog offer (basesync-generator-catalog): which generated files were already put to the operator, so the detector never re-offers them. Written by the /tp-merge-from-main offer site.

offered_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the offer was last recorded.

declined.description: True if the operator declined adding the offered generators.

offered_paths.description: Repo-relative generated paths already offered — deduped and sorted.

gitignore.description: First-run offer (c) state (consumer-offers.md): the .handoffs/ ignore rule. An absent key means not declined.

handoffs_declined.description: True if the operator declined the .handoffs/ ignore rule. Settles first-run condition 8 alongside a present rule; never re-asked.

worktree_immunization.description: Seat immunization state: tracks whether the heal-core-bare hook + extensions.worktreeConfig have been offered, applied, or declined. Mirrors the branch_protection block shape so the first-run preflight can check it with a single config-read condition.

offered_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the immunization offer was last shown to the operator.

applied_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when immunization was successfully applied (heal hooks installed + extensions.worktreeConfig=true set). Null if not yet applied.

declined.description: True if the operator explicitly declined immunization. Permanently suppresses the offer so first-run never re-asks.

test.description: Test infrastructure recorded by /tp-test-setup: the command, the runner family, and when it was last captured. Absent = not yet configured.

command.description: The canonical test command for this repo (e.g. `pytest -q`). Null = not recorded yet. The --exec lanes run it through the shell; per-node Targets verification runs a pytest command as one argv with no shell and accepts only plain words or quoted strings with no backslash, $, backtick, quote or newline inside, refusing anything else (an operator, redirect, glob, $, ~, a backtick, #, a backslash, a NAME= prefix) as runner-needs-shell naming the first offending character.

runner.description: The test-runner family. `pytest` for the pytest suite; `other` for any non-pytest runner.

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the test setup was last recorded by /tp-test-setup. Null = not yet recorded.

design_run_backend.description: Which backend a design-run window (launch_design_run.py) starts its orchestrator on. `route` (the default, today's behaviour): the Homelab launcher plans the window's backend from the folder's routes row, so the run can end up hybrid with its main thread routed to a local model. `direct`: the window command carries the launcher's seat role (`CLAUDE_LAUNCHER_ROLE=seat`), which makes the launch direct (backend `claude`, no router env) and adds Remote Control — the S4 proof gate: `--direct` is opt-in until one run proves its Strata children still reach the router (`router_checks.py --since`: Strata requests > 0 and about 0 checks per request), recorded in the design's `decisions.md`, and only then is this key set to `direct`. Without a Homelab launcher in the launching env (`CLAUDE_LAUNCHER_OWNED` unset) the seat role is inert, so the launcher prints one `W:` line and launches plain `claude`. NOT the model key: `models.design_run` is the `claude --model` argv; this key is the backend.

design_run_mcp.description: Which MCP servers a design-run window (launch_design_run.py) loads. The window starts with `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '<json>'` carrying only the servers named in `allow`, so an unused server (claude.ai Notion is ~60 tools) does not widen every turn's cached prefix. An absent block, or an empty `allow`, loads none. Read by skills/_shared/design_run_mcp.py; a Claude Code build without `--strict-mcp-config` leaves the command unchanged with one readout line.

allow.description: MCP server names to load into a design run (looked up in the project `.mcp.json` and the profile's `.claude.json`). Default `[]` = load none. A name with no definition on disk is reported on the launch readout, never fatal.

models.description: Per-role model selections. review/fix/classifier take a Q2 alias (dispatched via the Agent tool's call-time `model` parameter); design_run takes a `claude --model` argv (an alias or a full claude-* id). Shape-checked at validation to the alias enum here; the fuller shape (one of the four or ^claude-[a-z0-9.-]+$, either optionally suffixed exactly [1m], never inherit) is enforced by model_policy.validate_models. The cheap-tier slot keys (cheap_tier.SLOTS) each take one rung from their enum and are read by cheap_tier.load_slots, never by model_policy.

review.description: Model the review angle dispatches with. Exactly the Q2 alias set; no inherit (the Agent enum has no such value) and no full claude-* id.

fix.description: Model the fix-comments dispatch uses. Exactly the Q2 alias set.

classifier.description: Model the findings classifier dispatches with. Exactly the Q2 alias set.

design_run.description: A `claude --model` argv for a full design run: one of the four aliases or a full claude-* id, either optionally suffixed exactly [1m]; default opus[1m] (model_policy.DEFAULTS). Any non-empty string passes here; the alias-or-id[1m] shape (never inherit) is checked by model_policy.validate_models.

task.description: Cheap-tier task lever (a presence switch): with --cheap-tier and no --local, local-eligible plan tasks start on sonnet-xhigh under task_verify and the tier ladder. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

runbook.description: Cheap-tier slot: the post-merge teardown run as plain code (no model), checked by the exit_code oracle on the post-state. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

base_sync_splice.description: Cheap-tier slot: a base-sync splice proposal (never applied), checked by the zero_drop oracle. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

pr_fix_reproducer.description: Cheap-tier slot: a tp-pr-fix reproducer fix in a scratch worktree, checked by the reproducer_fixed oracle. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

classifier_judge.description: Cheap-tier slot: the findings classifier judge, checked by the classifier_schema oracle. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

history_line.description: Cheap-tier slot: a history-line draft, checked by the prose_shape oracle; a failed draft is dropped. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

handoff.description: Cheap-tier slot: a session handoff draft, checked by the prose_shape oracle; a failed draft is dropped. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

docs_draft.description: Cheap-tier slot: a living-docs draft, checked by the prose_shape oracle; a failed draft is dropped. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

review_slice.description: Cheap-tier slot: a tp-pr-iterate round's diff-slice prep, checked by the hunk_bytes oracle; a failed draft is dropped. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

review_refs.description: Cheap-tier slot: a tp-pr-iterate round's cross-reference prep, checked by the path_line oracle; a failed draft is dropped. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

ci_log_triage.description: Cheap-tier slot: a tp-pr-iterate round's CI-log triage, checked by the log_substring oracle; a failed draft is dropped. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

repro_scaffold.description: Cheap-tier slot: a tp-pr-iterate reproducer scaffold, checked by the observed_red oracle; a failed draft is dropped. Takes effect only with the --cheap-tier run flag (on by default); unset uses the slot's shipped rung ("off" opts the slot out; handoff ships off). Checked by cheap_tier.load_slots, not model_policy.

cheap_tier.description: Repo-level cheap-tier run defaults, resolved by skills/_shared/cheap_tier_default.py (never by cheap_tier.load_slots) at launch_design_run.py, /tp-merge-from-main, /tp-post-merge and the fleet launch lines; /tp-pr-iterate and /tp-pr-fix stay explicit-only. Absent (the default) means on.

default_run_flag.description: The --cheap-tier mode cheap_tier_default.py resolves when a run names none (on = the bare flag). Unset = on (the cheap tier is the default); "off" opts the repo out. An explicit --cheap-tier wins and --no-cheap-tier skips it for one run.

commit_guard.description: Commit-guard installation state: offered/applied/declined timestamps and booleans, the file-size cap opt-in, and the --no-verify deny-rule opt-in. Mirrors the worktree_immunization block shape.

offered_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the commit-guard offer was last shown. Null if never offered.

applied_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the commit guard was applied. Null if not yet applied.

declined.description: True if the operator declined the commit guard. Permanently suppresses the offer so first-run never re-asks.

file_size.description: Whether the file-size cap predicate (framework-check.sh invariant #34 + the file-size-guard hook) is enabled for this repo.

deny_no_verify.description: Whether the permissions.deny rule blocking `git commit --no-verify` is installed for this repo.

fragility.description: Test-fragility lint settings (fragility_lint.py). Absent block = registry defaults.

merge_predicate.description: Whether the merge gate folds the fragility_clear predicate (fragility_predicate.roster_block). True by default; only a literal false opts out, and the roster then shows fragility_clear as OMITTED (skipped (opt-out)) rather than dropping it.

gating_rules.description: Rule ids that gate (exit 1) in place of the registry's default gating set; an unknown id is a config error (exit 2).

strict.description: Strict mode of the fragility gate, read by the commit-time gate and by the merge gate's fragility_clear predicate (an unverified changed-tests run then fails instead of passing with a note). False by default.
